overview: A group runs its own copy of CivicOS to investigate how a government is meeting its obligations. Members bring documents in with a record of where each came from. They ask questions and support each answer with passages from those documents. A project concludes a question on the support it accepts, and the concluded question becomes a finding. The group publishes its findings as a case, in editions.

Then the group decides what to do. From the first suspicion, a project can open an action plan: the matters it is about and how well each is shown, the options open to it (a records request, a complaint, a story, testimony, a filing through counsel, and so on), which it chooses and which it declines with a reason, and up to three scenarios with checkpoints the group judges. Choosing an option starts an action, addressed to an office, an outlet or an organisation, never a private person. The assistant may draft what is sent; a member approves it and sends it by their own hand. The group then tracks replies and deadlines and, for a breach, the seven-stage escalation until compliance is restored.

Three things run through all of it. The record always says what is not known and why. It keeps track of who looked where and what they found. And the assistant finds, proposes and drafts, but a person makes every judgement and takes every act that commits the group.

displayPrimitives.name: The measures map: letters grade evidence, bars show progress, weights mark acts
displayPrimitives.meaning: one frame for every scale a member meets. One visual form per scale, used everywhere and for nothing else; colour marks the scale, never the value; every mark opens to its plain question; an answer is only as strong as the weakest thing it depends on; a grade tells how easily someone else could check it, never whether it is true
displayPrimitives.where: every grade, bar and act button

displayPrimitives.name: Undetermined (one component, always 'because…')
displayPrimitives.meaning: what we do not know and why: one component with a fixed mark, identical everywhere, and a mandatory 'because…' line; first-class, never an error, never a zero, written as a named term. A newcomer meets it first, beside strength against the bar
displayPrimitives.where: legs, strength axes, capture route, risk tier, standard source and in-force, consequences, home sets, deliverer, profiles, a stage the record cannot read

displayPrimitives.name: Its four neighbours: Withheld, Unrated, Nobody looked, Refused
displayPrimitives.meaning: each visibly different from Undetermined and from each other, each with one fixed sentence pattern of its own, never shared: Withheld (exists, not yours to see; incompleteness only, never what or how many); Unrated (nothing graded yet: rests on nothing); Nobody looked (no one searched there; not the same as looked and absent); Refused (the system declined an act, naming its reason). None is dressed as an error
displayPrimitives.src: DEC-86; Interaction Constructs §U; DEC-36; strength R3; observation-log R1
displayPrimitives.where: wherever Undetermined can appear

displayPrimitives.name: Evidence letters A-D (one shared scale)
displayPrimitives.meaning: every evidence scale (capture, connection, testimony, subject match) shares one A-D meaning: A is easiest for someone else to check, D rests on a person's word. Each scale has its own colour and descriptive icon (document, link, speech, person) and the same badge shape; scales are never added up and never take disjoint letters
displayPrimitives.src: DEC-82; Interaction Constructs §M; System Design §4; entities R9; provenance R24-R27
displayPrimitives.where: captures, subject matches, connections, legs, flow instances

displayPrimitives.name: Strength pair and the bar
displayPrimitives.meaning: the weakest capture and weakest connection, side by side, testimony beside; graded, 'Unrated' or 'Undetermined' with its reason; never one score. In the project workspace each question shows its two badges and one phrase against the bar ('Meets the bar', 'Short on connection', 'Short on capture', 'Unrated'); hover names the weakest document or link and how to raise it; 'Unrated' has its own treatment and fixed sentence, distinct from Undetermined (DEC-86)

displayPrimitives.name: Progress bars (stage, readiness, source identity)
displayPrimitives.meaning: each ladder has its own colour family and texture (solid, striped, dotted); dashed means 'not yet evaluated'; every step is named, reached or not. A project's stage stacks one bar per stage reached; hover, focus or tap discloses more and a click on a reached step shows how it was reached; 'closed' shows its reason and never reads as a finished stack. Readiness shows each rung by its own evidence; a published case reads Distributed, never Draft

Friction follows the rung: reversible inline; reasoned a reason field in place; terminal and attested a full dialog stating what ends or cannot be silently undone, and who signs; irreversible only through the ceremony. An act whose effect cannot be taken back outside the record opens the full dialog whatever its rung. An act with no rung is treated as reasoned

glossary.plain: The people who run one copy of CivicOS together; it can be one person.
The group's own installation, in the group's own hosting account.
glossary.avoidConfusionWith: a copy of a document (a capture)

glossary.plain: The person who claimed the copy first; the root of trust.
A person enrolled in the group with a handle and password.
A member who manages membership and group settings, but has no power inside a project they have not joined.
A permission a member holds, such as contribute; without it the act is not shown.
A one-time link that lets a new person enrol; once used it is gone.
A shared workspace where some members build a case together; hidden unless made discoverable.
glossary.avoidConfusionWith: a question: a project holds questions, it is not one

glossary.plain: A project member who can invite, remove and publish for that project.
A member who has joined a project and may act inside it.
Anything the group holds as evidence: a captured page or file, or a member's own written observation.
Fetching a public document and keeping its exact bytes, with where and when they came from.
glossary.avoidConfusionWith: capture grade (how well the capture is established)

glossary.plain: A named member states a document appears to be what it claims; not that it is true.
glossary.avoidConfusionWith: publish: releasing keeps it inside the group

glossary.plain: Take a document out of use; it is kept forever but can no longer be cited.
The record of where a document came from and how it reached the group.

A letter for how easily someone else could check something for themselves, never whether it is true. Capture, connection, testimony and subject match share one A-D meaning, each with its own colour and icon, and are never added up.
glossary.avoidConfusionWith: strength, which is the weakest grade along a chain

glossary.plain: A marked part of a document (a page region or text span) that can be cited on its own.
What the system extracted from a document's bytes, with how reliable that extraction is.
glossary.avoidConfusionWith: reading of a question's evidence (a basis version), which the old UI also calls a reading

glossary.plain: A member typing what part of a document says; it counts more once a different member confirms it.
A person, office, place, law or thing the record knows by name and aliases.
A link between documents through a shared subject, found by the machine or chosen by a member.
A member's own idea with a test that material passes or fails; it gathers material but never proves anything.
How something is supposed to go, as ordered stages, so a missing or late stage shows up.
A member's tip or suspicion and where to look; never evidence itself.
Something a member saw or heard, recorded in their own words as a document.
glossary.avoidConfusionWith: observation (a look: whether anyone looked and what they found)

glossary.plain: A record of whether anyone looked for something and what they found: 'Nobody looked', looked and absent, could not tell, present. 'Nobody looked' has its own look and fixed sentence, distinct from Undetermined ('could not tell', DEC-86).
glossary.avoidConfusionWith: firsthand observation

glossary.plain: Something the group is trying to answer, and the evidence it rests on.
A question the group has answered, with what would prove the answer wrong.
glossary.avoidConfusionWith: 'Noticed': the queue class for something the system noticed that nobody has judged (K356)

glossary.plain: One piece of evidence cited for or against a question.
Add a piece of evidence to a question, or withdraw it with a reason; withdrawn evidence stays listed.
One way of arranging a question's evidence; members accept or turn it down, and a project picks one to stand on.
glossary.avoidConfusionWith: reading of a document (extraction)

glossary.plain: How well a question is supported: the weakest capture and weakest connection, shown as a pair, never one score.
glossary.avoidConfusionWith: grade: strength is read off the weakest grade

glossary.plain: The strength a project (or the group by default) requires before it will publish.
What we do not know, and why: one mark with a line that always says 'because…', shown the same way everywhere, never as an error or a zero (DEC-86).
glossary.avoidConfusionWith: its four neighbours, each with its own look and its own fixed sentence, never shared (DEC-86): withheld (it exists, you may not see it), unrated (nothing graded yet), nobody looked, refused (the system declined an act)

glossary.plain: The group's or project's stated viewpoint, adopted openly so readers can weigh it.
Bias debt: the lens changed since work was done, disclosed. Hunch debt: a connection graded ahead of its evidence, must be cleared before publishing.

glossary.plain: What a project publishes: a set of findings and evidence, signed, that anyone can check.
glossary.avoidConfusionWith: a question or finding (before DEC-72 a case was a phase of a question)

glossary.plain: An unsigned draft of a case shown to chosen reviewers inside the group; never leaves.
glossary.avoidConfusionWith: publication

glossary.plain: The case's statement of what it leaves out; others confirm they read it.

An owner signs with a registered key: the case document, then each finding and its evidence. Decided: signing happens in the browser with a browser-held key, producing the same signature strangers check.
glossary.avoidConfusionWith: release (vouching needs no key)

glossary.plain: Put a case across the fence for anyone to read, through the publication ceremony; it cannot be taken back, only corrected by a new edition.
Anyone checks a published case against its hash without the group's help.
A rule, law or commitment the group holds in its own words, with its source and period.
A member's judgement of whether a government act complied with named standards: complies, does not, or unclear.
glossary.avoidConfusionWith: finding: a determination rests on findings

glossary.plain: The harm or cost of a breach, computed from the record, assessed by a member, or undetermined.
Something the group asks of someone outside it, with the reply, the clock and the correspondence.

glossary.plain: A prepared request or complaint text, and a bundle of facts assembled for a lawyer; not legal advice.

A deadline on an action, always with the law or promise it comes from.
Everything that wants a member, grouped by case: to-dos, things noticed, and signals.

A request for the system to fetch a public address later, which the source may refuse.
Material handed over through the doorbell by someone without an account, waiting for a member to decide. Its source is an unnamed knocker, never 'unknown'.

A notice that something your work rests on changed, asking for a second look.
Re-checking a document's public address on a schedule to see if it changed or vanished.
Local rules and deadlines for a place, chosen by an administrator.
A signing key proves who signed; an assistant key lets a machine act; a source login opens a paywalled source.
The sequence of acts a finding passes on its way out: release, stand behind, ground, conclude, accept, ratify, publish.

otherRulings.title: A project's stage and its cases' readiness
otherRulings.decided: 'closed' stays the owner's recorded act with its judged reason; the other three stages are always computed. Each readiness rung shows by its own evidence; a published case reads Distributed, never Draft ('newspapers don't publish drafts'); Internally checked and Externally compliant read 'not yet evaluated' until the evaluations exist.

otherRulings.title: What a member reads when an act is refused
otherRulings.decided: The standard sentence, followed by the act's own specific next step or alternative, shown to the member, never a hidden field; BOB reads it as the pattern for every refusal that shares a code.

otherRulings.title: Thirteen points on presenting and resolving a contradiction
otherRulings.decided: All as recommended, two revised: an undetermined candidate is a lead; a record duty binds every project drawing on either side until resolved; two projects' different conclusions are plurality unless they cannot both hold in the same respect; the question's own conclusion resolves it; the machine recommends only which respects may differ; a stale side moves nothing by itself; a hypothesised cause is published as 'cause not established'; an irreconcilable conclusion is disclosed; publication discloses, never blocks; accepting keeps the machine's reason the machine's; 'one of them is wrong' needs a written reason; a dismissal gives one fixed reason.
